crises.title: Money Problems Get Very Bad
crises.description: Shops are closing, many people can't find work, and it's getting hard to buy food and other basic things. The area's money situation has hit rock bottom.

options.text: Cut spending and save money

advisors.economist: We need to spend less. It hurts now but stops things getting worse.
advisors.ranger: Cutting green projects will hurt the land even more.
advisors.monk: Sharing the hard times can bring people together, or tear them apart.

options.text: Start big community work projects

advisors.economist: Putting people to work puts money in their hands.
advisors.ranger: Machines for jobs will still knock down old trees.
advisors.monk: Working together can help heal people's hearts.

crises.title: Losing Our Ways of Life
crises.description: Old traditions are being forgotten, languages are disappearing, and young people are moving away from the values of their ancestors.

options.text: Make schools teach our culture

advisors.economist: Time spent in classes is time not spent working.
advisors.ranger: The names of plants and animals live in old words.
advisors.monk: We must plant wisdom early so it grows deep.

options.text: Help traditional craft makers and performers

advisors.economist: Paying for this will drain our money.
advisors.ranger: Natural dyes and woven reeds are good for the earth.
advisors.monk: Making things with care keeps our past alive.

crises.title: Problems with How We're Run
crises.description: Local leaders are seen as dishonest and slow, and people have lost faith in them.

options.text: Fire dishonest officials

advisors.economist: Firing people creates empty seats and worry.
advisors.ranger: A clean stream runs clear after a flood.
advisors.monk: Cutting the rotten branch saves the tree.

options.text: Let villages make more of their own choices

advisors.economist: Local people know what they need.
advisors.ranger: Villages protect their own forests best.
advisors.monk: Sharing trust with many builds a stronger home.

crises.title: People Are Angry and Fighting
crises.description: Protests are turning into fights, and the streets are full of anger. People are demanding change, but chaos is spreading.

options.text: Talk with protest leaders

advisors.economist: Talking costs less than fixing broken windows.
advisors.ranger: Peace in the valleys lets seeds grow.
advisors.monk: Listening is the first step to understanding.

options.text: Use force to stop them

advisors.economist: We need order before we can make money.
advisors.ranger: Violence hurts the peace of the wild.
advisors.monk: A fist cannot hold the truth.

crises.title: Nature Is in Big Trouble
crises.description: Cutting too many trees, pollution, and changing weather are pushing nature to the breaking point. Floods and droughts are happening more often.

options.text: Make tough rules to protect nature

advisors.economist: Rules hold back business.
advisors.ranger: Finally, the forest gets protection.
advisors.monk: Taking care of life is our most important duty.

options.text: Spend on green projects and planting trees

advisors.economist: Green jobs are still jobs.
advisors.ranger: Planting a tree is planting hope.
advisors.monk: Healing the earth heals the mind.

crises.title: Big Cheating Scandal Revealed
crises.description: A huge cheating ring has been found, with officials and business people involved. Trust in leaders is broken.

options.text: Take all of them to court

advisors.economist: Trials make people scared to invest.
advisors.ranger: Justice, like rain, cleans the air.
advisors.monk: Bad actions must be faced, not hidden.

options.text: Forgive and fix the system

advisors.economist: Peace returns faster if we forgive.
advisors.ranger: A wound half-healed will still hurt.
advisors.monk: Showing mercy opens the door to change.

crises.title: People Don't Trust Leaders
crises.description: The public has lost all faith in the government and other groups. Few people want to take part in civic life.

options.text: Be more open and talk with citizens

advisors.economist: Talking costs money and makes no direct profit.
advisors.ranger: Open skies hide no storms.
advisors.monk: Speaking plainly builds a bridge.

options.text: Create outside groups to watch over things

advisors.economist: More groups mean more paperwork.
advisors.ranger: Watchers in the tower see the smoke early.
advisors.monk: Outside eyes see what inside eyes miss.

crises.title: Other Countries Have Too Much Power Here
crises.description: Outside powers are controlling too much of our politics and money, threatening our freedom to make our own choices.

options.text: Change agreements and rely less on them

advisors.economist: Changing deals might make trade harder.
advisors.ranger: A bird in its own nest sings freely.
advisors.monk: Being independent is key to self-respect.

options.text: Take back foreign-owned businesses

advisors.economist: Taking things still needs people who know how to run them.
advisors.ranger: What was taken once is taken again.
advisors.monk: Grabbing creates more grabbing.

crises.title: Nature Falls Apart
crises.description: The environment is very badly damaged, and natural disasters are hurting communities. The situation is really bad.

options.text: Emergency move people to safety

advisors.economist: Moving people costs less than moving mountains.
advisors.ranger: Leaving the land leaves behind its spirit.
advisors.monk: Even things that don't last deserve a good goodbye.

options.text: Huge project to fix nature

advisors.economist: Fixing nature is a bet on future harvests.
advisors.ranger: The forest remembers those who come to heal it.
advisors.monk: Fixing what is broken is the deepest practice.

crises.title: People Rebel Because They Don't Trust Leaders
crises.description: Angry people don't trust those in charge, and protests are becoming acts of rebellion.

options.text: Talk and make peace with communities

advisors.economist: Talking doesn't fill empty stomachs.
advisors.ranger: A circle of voices is stronger than a wall.
advisors.monk: Making peace is built one talk at a time.

options.text: Send more police and set curfews

advisors.economist: Spending on security is a necessary cost.
advisors.ranger: Cages don't tame the wild, they just hide it.
advisors.monk: Fear is a bad foundation for peace.

crises.title: Money Troubles and Outside Control
crises.description: Our weak money situation lets other countries control us, leading to being taken advantage of and loss of freedom.

options.text: Control money flow and limit trade

advisors.economist: Walls around money hurt the market.
advisors.ranger: A closed valley keeps its water, but also its floods.
advisors.monk: Holding on too tight often brings chaos.

options.text: Find many different country partners

advisors.economist: Many ropes are harder to cut than one.
advisors.ranger: A forest with many trees survives the storm.
advisors.monk: Balance comes from many, not one.

crises.title: Losing Our Way and Good Leadership
crises.description: Both our cultural identity and how we are governed are getting worse fast. The fabric of society is coming apart.

options.text: Bring back culture and fix how we're run

advisors.economist: Fixing things is costly and slow.
advisors.ranger: Deep roots hold the soil against any wind.
advisors.monk: Renewing tradition and rules is the middle way.

options.text: Join with a nearby area for stability

advisors.economist: Coming together lowers costs.
advisors.ranger: Two rivers joined lose their separate songs.
advisors.monk: Giving up who we are for comfort is not peace.

crises.title: Who Are We? Trust and Culture Are Slipping
crises.description: With trust in leaders crumbling and cultural pride fading, society is losing its sense of togetherness. We need to act now.

options.text: Hold a 'Proud of Our Roots' festival and teach civic values

advisors.economist: Festivals bring in tourists and spending.
advisors.ranger: Celebrating where we live reminds us why it matters.
advisors.monk: Joy in our heritage shines a light in the dark.

options.text: Create village councils with real power

advisors.economist: Sharing power speeds some choices, slows others.
advisors.ranger: Those who live in the forest should guide its care.
advisors.monk: Power shared is power multiplied.

crises.title: Not Enough Resources and Money Problems
crises.description: Using up too much of nature has destroyed forests and rivers, hurting both the economy and the environment.

options.text: Set limits on taking resources and support green business

advisors.economist: Limits hurt now but help later.
advisors.ranger: Take only what grows back—that's nature's rule.
advisors.monk: Saving today means having more tomorrow.

options.text: Let foreign companies take resources for quick cash

advisors.economist: Quick cash fixes the leak today.
advisors.ranger: Selling the mountain leaves only a hole.
advisors.monk: Doing things out of fear often leads to regret.
